   104→def _load_json_object(path: Path, *, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
   105→    if not path.exists():
   106→        raise CommandError(f"Error: {label} not found: {path}")
   107→    try:
   108→        payload = json.loads(path.read_text())
   109→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   110→        raise CommandError(f"Error: failed reading {label}: {exc}") from exc
   111→    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
   112→        raise CommandError(f"Error: {label} must contain a JSON object.")
   113→    return payload
   114→
   115→
   116→def _session_payload(session_id: str) -> tuple[Path, dict[str, Any]]:
   117→    _validate_session_id(session_id)
   118→    path = _session_file(session_id)
   119→    payload = _load_json_object(path, label="session")
   120→    payload_id = str(payload.get("session_id", "")).strip()
   121→    if payload_id != session_id:
   122→        raise CommandError(
   123→            f"Error: session id mismatch in {path} (expected {session_id}, found {payload_id or '<missing>'}).",
   124→        )
   125→    return path, payload

   133→    config: dict[str, Any],

   135→    """Prepare holistic review packet and persist immutable+blind snapshots."""
   136→    context = resolve_review_packet_context(args)

   138→    try:
   139→        packet = build_review_packet_payload(

   147→    except ValueError as exc:
   148→        msg = str(exc).strip()
   149→        if not msg:

   151→        raise CommandError(msg, exit_code=1) from exc
   152→    write_query(packet)

   162→    )
   163→    return packet, packet_path, blind_path

   183→def _build_claude_launch_prompt(
   184→    *,
   185→    session_id: str,
   186→    token: str,
   187→    blind_path: Path,
   188→    template_path: Path,
   189→    output_path: Path,
   190→    packet: dict[str, Any],
   191→) -> str:
   192→    """Build a copy/paste-ready prompt for a Claude blind reviewer subagent."""
   193→    header = (
   194→        "# Claude Blind Reviewer Launch Prompt\n\n"
   195→        "You are an isolated blind reviewer. Do not use prior chat context, "
   196→        "prior score history, or target-score anchoring.\n\n"
   197→        f"Session id: {session_id}\n"
   198→        f"Session token: {token}\n"
   199→        f"Blind packet: {blind_path}\n"
   200→        f"Template JSON: {template_path}\n"
   201→        f"Output JSON path: {output_path}\n\n"
   202→    )
   203→
   204→    raw_batches = packet.get("investigation_batches", [])
   205→    if not isinstance(raw_batches, list):
   206→        raw_batches = []
   207→    raw_dim_prompts = packet.get("dimension_prompts")
   208→    dim_prompts: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = (
   209→        raw_dim_prompts if isinstance(raw_dim_prompts, dict) else {}
   210→    )
   211→    batches = explode_to_single_dimension(
   212→        [b for b in raw_batches if isinstance(b, dict)],
   213→        dimension_prompts=dim_prompts or None,
   214→    )
   215→
   216→    all_dims: set[str] = set()
   217→    combined_cap = 0
   218→    batch_sections: list[str] = []
   219→    for i, batch in enumerate(batches):
   220→        ctx = build_batch_context(batch, i)
   221→        all_dims.update(ctx.dimension_set)
   222→        combined_cap += ctx.issues_cap
   223→
   224→        section = (
   225→            f"--- Batch {i + 1}: {ctx.name} ---\n"
   226→            f"Rationale: {ctx.rationale}\n"
   227→        )
   228→        section += render_dimension_prompts_block(ctx.dimensions, dim_prompts)
   229→        section += render_seed_files_block(ctx)
   230→        section += render_historical_focus(batch)
   231→        section += render_mechanical_concern_signals(batch)
   232→        batch_sections.append(section)
   233→
   234→    if not combined_cap:
   235→        combined_cap = 10
   236→
   237→    output_schema = (
   238→        "Output schema:\n"
   239→        "{\n"
   240→        '  "session": {"id": "<preserve from template>", "token": "<preserve from template>"},\n'
   241→        '  "assessments": {"<dimension>": <0-100 with one decimal place>},\n'
   242→        '  "dimension_notes": {\n'
   243→        '    "<dimension>": {\n'
   244→        '      "evidence": ["specific code observations"],\n'
   245→        '      "impact_scope": "local|module|subsystem|codebase",\n'
   246→        '      "fix_scope": "single_edit|multi_file_refactor|architectural_change",\n'
   247→        '      "confidence": "high|medium|low"\n'
   248→        "    }\n"
   249→        "  },\n"
   250→        '  "issues": [{\n'
   251→        '    "dimension": "<dimension>",\n'
   252→        '    "identifier": "short_id",\n'
   253→        '    "summary": "one-line defect summary",\n'
   254→        '    "related_files": ["relative/path.py"],\n'
   255→        '    "evidence": ["specific code observation"],\n'
   256→        '    "suggestion": "concrete fix recommendation",\n'
   257→        '    "confidence": "high|medium|low",\n'
   258→        '    "impact_scope": "local|module|subsystem|codebase",\n'
   259→        '    "fix_scope": "single_edit|multi_file_refactor|architectural_change",\n'
   260→        '    "root_cause_cluster": "optional_cluster_name"\n'
   261→        "  }]\n"
   262→        "}\n\n"
   263→    )
   264→
   265→    session_requirements = (
   266→        "Session requirements:\n"
   267→        f"1. Keep `session.id` exactly `{session_id}`.\n"
   268→        f"2. Keep `session.token` exactly `{token}`.\n"
   269→        "3. Do not include provenance metadata (CLI injects canonical provenance).\n"
   270→    )
   271→
   272→    from desloppify.engine.plan_state import load_policy_result, render_policy_block
   273→
   274→    policy_result = load_policy_result()
   275→    policy_text = render_policy_block(policy_result.policy)
   276→    if not policy_result.ok:
   277→        print(
   278→            colorize(
   279→                f"  Warning: ignoring malformed project policy ({policy_result.message or 'unknown error'}).",
   280→                "yellow",
   281→            )
   282→        )
   283→
   284→    return join_non_empty_sections(
   285→        header,
   286→        *batch_sections,
   287→        policy_text,
   288→        render_scoring_frame(),
   289→        render_scan_evidence_note(),
   290→        render_task_requirements(issues_cap=combined_cap, dim_set=all_dims),
   291→        render_scope_enums(),
   292→        output_schema,
   293→        session_requirements,

   419→def _canonical_external_payload(
   420→    raw_payload: dict[str, Any],
   421→    *,
   422→    session: dict[str, Any],
   423→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   424→    """Return import payload with canonical provenance and required session token."""
   425→    session_meta = raw_payload.get("session")
   426→    if not isinstance(session_meta, dict):
   427→        raise CommandError(
   428→            "Error: external reviewer payload must include top-level `session` object."
   429→            ' Expected: {"session":{"id":"...","token":"..."},"assessments":{...},"issues":[...]}',
   430→        )
   431→
   432→    payload_id = str(session_meta.get("id", "")).strip()
   433→    payload_token = str(session_meta.get("token", "")).strip()
   434→    expected_id = str(session.get("session_id", "")).strip()
   435→    expected_token = str(session.get("token", "")).strip()
   436→    if payload_id != expected_id or payload_token != expected_token:
   437→        raise CommandError(
   438→            "Error: session id/token mismatch in external reviewer payload."
   439→            " Regenerate output using the session template/instructions.",
   440→        )
   441→
   442→    payload = {
   443→        key: value
   444→        for key, value in raw_payload.items()
   445→        if key not in {"session", "provenance"}
   446→    }
   447→    payload["provenance"] = {
   448→        "kind": "blind_review_batch_import",
   449→        "blind": True,
   450→        "runner": str(session.get("runner", "claude")),
   451→        "session_id": str(session.get("session_id", "")),
   452→        "created_at": _iso_seconds(_utc_now()),
   453→        "packet_path": str(session.get("blind_packet_path", "")),
   454→        "packet_sha256": str(session.get("packet_sha256", "")),
   455→    }
   456→    return payload
   457→
   458→
   459→def _ensure_session_open(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   460→    status = str(session.get("status", "open")).strip().lower()
   461→    if status == "open":
   462→        return
   463→    raise CommandError(
   464→        f"Error: session is not open (status={status or 'unknown'}). Start a new session with --external-start.",
   465→    )
   466→
   467→
   468→def _ensure_session_not_expired(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   469→    expires_at = _parse_iso(session.get("expires_at"))
   470→    if expires_at is None:
   471→        raise CommandError(
   472→            "Error: session metadata is missing/invalid expires_at.",
   473→        )
   474→    now = _utc_now()
   475→    if now <= expires_at:
   476→        return
   477→    raise CommandError(
   478→        f"Error: session expired at {session.get('expires_at')}. Start a new session with --external-start.",
   479→    )

   482→def do_external_submit(
   483→    *,
   484→    import_file: str,
   485→    session_id: str,
   486→    state: dict,
   487→    lang,
   488→    state_file,
   489→    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   490→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   491→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   492→    scan_path: str = ".",
   493→    dry_run: bool = False,
   494→) -> None:
   495→    """Submit external reviewer output via session, adding canonical provenance."""
   496→    config = config or {}
   497→    session_path, session = _session_payload(session_id)
   498→    _ensure_session_open(session)
   499→    _ensure_session_not_expired(session)
   500→
   501→    if str(session.get("runner", "")).strip().lower() not in _EXTERNAL_SUPPORTED_RUNNERS:
   502→        raise CommandError(
   503→            "Error: only Claude external sessions currently support durable score submit.",
   504→        )
   505→
   506→    issues_path = Path(import_file)
   507→    raw_payload = _load_json_object(issues_path, label="external issues")
   508→    canonical_payload = _canonical_external_payload(raw_payload, session=session)
   509→
   510→    stamp = run_stamp()
   511→    session_dir = session_path.parent
   512→    canonical_path = session_dir / f"canonical_import_{stamp}.json"
   513→    safe_write_text(canonical_path, json.dumps(canonical_payload, indent=2) + "\n")
   514→
   515→    _import_config = ReviewImportConfig(
   516→        config=config,
   517→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   518→        attested_external=True,
   519→        manual_attest=str(session.get("attest", EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT)),
   520→    )
   521→
   522→    if dry_run:
   523→        do_validate_import(
   524→            str(canonical_path),
   525→            lang,
   526→            import_config=_import_config,
   527→        )
   528→        return
   529→
   530→    do_import(
   531→        str(canonical_path),
   532→        state,
   533→        lang,
   534→        state_file,
   535→        import_config=_import_config,
   536→    )
   537→
   538→    submitted_at = _iso_seconds(_utc_now())
   539→    session["status"] = "submitted"
   540→    session["submitted_at"] = submitted_at
   541→    session["submitted_input_file"] = str(issues_path)
   542→    session["submitted_canonical_file"] = str(canonical_path)
   543→    safe_write_text(session_path, json.dumps(session, indent=2) + "\n")
   544→
   545→    if scan_after_import:
   546→        code = run_followup_scan(
   547→            lang_name=lang.name,
   548→            scan_path=scan_path,
   549→            deps=FollowupScanDeps(
   550→                project_root=_runtime_project_root(),
   551→                timeout_seconds=FOLLOWUP_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   552→                python_executable=sys.executable,
   553→                subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
   554→                timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
   555→                colorize_fn=colorize,
   556→            ),
   557→        )
   558→        if code != 0:
   559→            raise CommandError(f"External review exited with code {code}", exit_code=code)
   560→
   561→
   562→__all__ = ["do_external_start", "do_external_submit", "EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT"]
   563→

This is the key insight. There's a clear detector→dimension mapping. Findings from `structural` are relevant to `abstraction_fitness` and `design_coherence`. Findings from `coupling` are relevant to `cross_module_architecture`. But right now only the `design_coherence` batch gets concerns — the `abstraction_fitness`, `cross_module_architecture`, etc. batches see nothing.

The right approach: give **every** dimension batch a summary of the judgment findings relevant to its dimension, with CLI exploration commands. This doesn't require concerns (which are design_coherence-specific) — it requires surfacing the raw detector findings per-dimension.

So each batch just gets told "scan_evidence exists in the blind packet" — a vague pointer. They don't get told about specific detector findings for their dimension, don't get CLI commands to explore them, and have no mechanism to dismiss or confirm.

The fix: add a per-dimension judgment finding summary to every batch. This requires knowing which detectors map to which dimension, then injecting finding counts + CLI commands.

   164→            merged = False

   171→                            existing_files.add(filepath)
   172→                    existing["concern_signals"] = concerns_batch.get("concern_signals", [])

   174→                    jfc = concerns_batch.get("judgment_finding_counts")

   177→                    merged = True

    27→    file_cache: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    28→    batches: list[dict] = []
    29→
    30→    for dimension, collector_key in _DIMENSION_FILE_MAPPING.items():
    31→        if collector_key not in file_cache:

    54→def filter_batches_to_dimensions(
    55→    batches: list[dict],
    56→    dimensions: list[str],
    57→    *,
    58→    fallback_max_files: int | None = 80,
    59→) -> list[dict]:
    60→    """Keep only batches whose dimension is in the active set."""
    61→    selected = [dimension for dimension in dimensions if isinstance(dimension, str) and dimension]
    62→    if not selected:

    64→    selected_set = set(selected)
    65→    filtered: list[dict] = []

    69→        if not batch_dims:

    72→        covered.update(batch_dims)
    73→
    74→    missing = [dim for dim in selected if dim not in covered]
    75→    if not missing:

    77→

    88→    for dim in missing:

   100→def batch_concerns(
   101→    concerns: list,
   102→    *,
   103→    max_files: int | None = None,
   104→    active_dimensions: list[str] | None = None,
   105→) -> dict | None:
   106→    """Build investigation batch from mechanical concern signals."""
   107→    del active_dimensions
   108→    if not concerns:
   109→        return None
   110→
   111→    types = sorted({concern.type for concern in concerns if concern.type})
   112→    why_parts = ["mechanical detectors identified structural patterns needing judgment"]
   113→    if types:
   114→        why_parts.append(f"concern types: {', '.join(types)}")
   115→
   116→    files: list[str] = []
   117→    seen: set[str] = set()
   118→    concern_signals: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   119→    for concern in concerns:
   120→        candidate = _normalize_file_path(getattr(concern, "file", ""))
   121→        if not candidate or candidate in seen:
   122→            continue
   123→        seen.add(candidate)
   124→        files.append(candidate)
   125→
   126→        evidence_raw = getattr(concern, "evidence", ())
   127→        evidence = [
   128→            str(entry).strip()
   129→            for entry in evidence_raw
   130→            if isinstance(entry, str) and entry.strip()
   131→        ][:4]
   132→        summary = str(getattr(concern, "summary", "")).strip()
   133→        question = str(getattr(concern, "question", "")).strip()
   134→        concern_type = str(getattr(concern, "type", "")).strip()
   135→        fingerprint = str(getattr(concern, "fingerprint", "")).strip()
   136→        source_issues = tuple(
   137→            str(sid)
   138→            for sid in getattr(concern, "source_issues", ())
   139→            if isinstance(sid, str) and sid
   140→        )
   141→        signal: dict[str, object] = {
   142→            "type": concern_type or "design_concern",
   143→            "file": candidate,
   144→            "summary": summary or "Mechanical concern requires subjective judgment",
   145→            "question": question or "Is this pattern intentional or debt?",
   146→            "evidence": evidence,
   147→        }
   148→        if fingerprint:
   149→            signal["fingerprint"] = fingerprint
   150→        if source_issues:
   151→            signal["finding_ids"] = list(source_issues)
   152→        concern_signals.append(signal)
   153→
   154→    total_candidate_files = len(files)
   155→    if (
   156→        max_files is not None
   157→        and isinstance(max_files, int)
   158→        and max_files > 0
   159→        and total_candidate_files > max_files
   160→    ):
   161→        files = files[:max_files]
   162→        why_parts.append(
   163→            f"truncated to {max_files} files from {total_candidate_files} candidates"
   164→        )
   165→
   166→    # Build per-detector judgment finding counts by extracting the detector name
   167→    # from each source issue ID (format: "detector::file::detail").
   168→    detector_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   169→    seen_source_ids: set[str] = set()
   170→    for concern in concerns:
   171→        for sid in getattr(concern, "source_issues", ()):
   172→            sid_str = str(sid)
   173→            if sid_str in seen_source_ids:
   174→                continue
   175→            seen_source_ids.add(sid_str)
   176→            detector = sid_str.split("::", 1)[0] if "::" in sid_str else ""
   177→            if detector:
   178→                detector_counts[detector] = detector_counts.get(detector, 0) + 1
   179→
   180→    result: dict[str, object] = {
   181→        "name": "design_coherence",
   182→        "dimensions": ["design_coherence"],
   183→        "files_to_read": files,
   184→        "why": "; ".join(why_parts),
   185→        "total_candidate_files": total_candidate_files,
   186→        "concern_signals": concern_signals,
   187→        "concern_signal_count": len(concern_signals),
   188→    }
   189→    if detector_counts:
   190→        result["judgment_finding_counts"] = detector_counts
   191→    return result
   192→

  "old_string": "__all__ = [\"batch_concerns\", \"build_investigation_batches\", \"filter_batches_to_dimensions\"]",
  "new_string": "# Mechanical detectors → subjective dimensions they provide evidence for.\n# Mirrors _DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS in engine/_state/merge.py.\n_DETECTOR_DIMENSIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n    \"structural\": (\"design_coherence\", \"abstraction_fitness\"),\n    \"smells\": (\"design_coherence\", \"error_consistency\"),\n    \"global_mutable_config\": (\"initialization_coupling\",),\n    \"coupling\": (\"cross_module_architecture\",),\n    \"layer_violation\": (\"cross_module_architecture\",),\n    \"private_imports\": (\"cross_module_architecture\",),\n    \"dupes\": (\"convention_outlier\",),\n    \"boilerplate_duplication\": (\"convention_outlier\",),\n    \"naming\": (\"convention_outlier\", \"naming_quality\"),\n    \"flat_dirs\": (\"package_organization\",),\n    \"orphaned\": (\"design_coherence\",),\n    \"uncalled_functions\": (\"design_coherence\",),\n    \"responsibility_cohesion\": (\"design_coherence\", \"abstraction_fitness\"),\n    \"cycles\": (\"cross_module_architecture\", \"dependency_health\"),\n    \"dict_keys\": (\"type_safety\",),\n    \"props\": (\"abstraction_fitness\",),\n    \"signature\": (\"convention_outlier\",),\n    \"security\": (\"error_consistency\",),\n}\n\n# Invert to dimension → set of detectors.\n_DIMENSION_DETECTORS: dict[str, set[str]] = {}\nfor _det, _dims in _DETECTOR_DIMENSIONS.items():\n    for _dim in _dims:\n        _DIMENSION_DETECTORS.setdefault(_dim, set()).add(_det)\n\n\ndef annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings(\n    batches: list[dict],\n    state: dict,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Add per-dimension judgment_finding_counts to batches that lack them.\n\n    For each batch, look at its dimension(s), find which detectors map to those\n    dimensions, count open judgment findings per detector from state, and inject\n    ``judgment_finding_counts`` so the prompt renderer can show CLI exploration\n    commands.  Batches that already have ``judgment_finding_counts`` (e.g. the\n    design_coherence concern batch) are left untouched.\n    \"\"\"\n    from desloppify.base.registry import JUDGMENT_DETECTORS\n\n    issues = state.get(\"issues\")\n    if not isinstance(issues, dict):\n        return\n\n    # Count open judgment findings per detector once.\n    global_detector_counts: dict[str, int] = {}\n    for issue in issues.values():\n        if not isinstance(issue, dict):\n            continue\n        status = str(issue.get(\"status\", \"\")).strip()\n        if status not in (\"open\", \"reopened\"):\n            continue\n        detector = str(issue.get(\"detector\", \"\")).strip()\n        if detector and detector in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS:\n            global_detector_counts[detector] = global_detector_counts.get(detector, 0) + 1\n\n    if not global_detector_counts:\n        return\n\n    for batch in batches:\n        if batch.get(\"judgment_finding_counts\"):\n            continue\n        dims = batch.get(\"dimensions\", [])\n        if not isinstance(dims, list):\n            continue\n        # Collect detectors relevant to this batch's dimensions.\n        relevant_detectors: set[str] = set()\n        for dim in dims:\n            relevant_detectors.update(_DIMENSION_DETECTORS.get(dim, ()))\n        if not relevant_detectors:\n            continue\n        counts = {\n            det: count\n            for det, count in global_detector_counts.items()\n            if det in relevant_detectors\n        }\n        if counts:\n            batch[\"judgment_finding_counts\"] = counts\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings\",\n    \"batch_concerns\",\n    \"build_investigation_batches\",\n    \"filter_batches_to_dimensions\",\n]"
}

    65→
    66→def module_patterns(content: str) -> list[str]:
    67→    """Return C#-specific module convention markers for a file."""
    68→    out: list[str] = []
    69→    if re.search(r"\bnamespace\s+[A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)*", content):
    70→        out.append("namespace")
    71→    if re.search(r"\b(?:public|internal)\s+(?:class|record|struct)\s+\w+", content):
    72→        out.append("public_types")
    73→    if re.search(r"\bpublic\s+.*\(", content):
    74→        out.append("public_methods")
    75→    return out
    76→
    77→
    78→def api_surface(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    79→    """Compute C# API-surface consistency context."""
    80→    sync_async_mix: list[str] = []
    81→    for filepath, content in file_contents.items():
    82→        has_sync = bool(re.search(r"\bpublic\s+(?:\w+\s+)+\w+\s*\(", content))
    83→        has_async = bool(
    84→            re.search(r"\bpublic\s+async\s+Task(?:<[^>]+>)?\s+\w+\s*\(", content)
    85→        )
    86→        if has_sync and has_async:
    87→            sync_async_mix.append(rel(filepath))
    88→    if not sync_async_mix:
    89→        return {}
    90→    return {"sync_async_mix": sync_async_mix[:20]}
    91→

    27→LOW_VALUE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"(?m)^\s*(?:signal|@tool)\b")
    28→
    29→_PATH_REF_RE = re.compile(
    30→    r"""(?:preload|load)\(\s*['"](?P<path>res://[^'"]+)['"]\s*\)|^\s*extends\s+['"](?P<extends>res://[^'"]+)['"]""",
    31→    re.MULTILINE,
    32→)
    33→_CLASS_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^\s*class_name\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)")
    34→_FUNC_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^\s*func\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\(")

    37→def module_patterns(content: str) -> list[str]:
    38→    """Extract module-level script references for review context."""
    39→    out: list[str] = []
    40→    for match in _PATH_REF_RE.finditer(content):
    41→        ref = match.group("path") or match.group("extends")
    42→        if ref:
    43→            out.append(ref)
    44→    return out
    45→
    46→
    47→def api_surface(file_contents: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    48→    """Build minimal API-surface summary from parsed GDScript files."""
    49→    classes: set[str] = set()
    50→    functions: set[str] = set()
    51→    for content in file_contents.values():
    52→        classes.update(match.group(1) for match in _CLASS_RE.finditer(content))
    53→        for match in _FUNC_RE.finditer(content):
    54→            name = match.group(1)
    55→            if not name.startswith("_"):
    56→                functions.add(name)
    57→    return {"classes": sorted(classes), "public_functions": sorted(functions)}

1→"""Top-level batch building APIs for holistic review preparation."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from .prepare_batches_collectors import _DIMENSION_FILE_MAPPING, _FILE_COLLECTORS
     8→from .prepare_batches_core import (
     9→    _collect_files_from_batches,
    10→    _ensure_holistic_context,
    11→    _normalize_file_path,
    12→)
    13→
    14→
    15→def build_investigation_batches(
    16→    holistic_ctx,
    17→    lang: object,
    18→    *,
    19→    repo_root: Path | None = None,
    20→    max_files_per_batch: int | None = None,
    21→) -> list[dict]:
    22→    """Build one batch per dimension from holistic context."""
    23→    ctx = _ensure_holistic_context(holistic_ctx)
    24→    del lang
    25→    del repo_root
    26→
    27→    file_cache: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    28→    batches: list[dict] = []
    29→
    30→    for dimension, collector_key in _DIMENSION_FILE_MAPPING.items():
    31→        if collector_key not in file_cache:
    32→            collector = _FILE_COLLECTORS[collector_key]
    33→            file_cache[collector_key] = collector(
    34→                ctx,
    35→                max_files=max_files_per_batch,
    36→            )
    37→
    38→        files = file_cache[collector_key]
    39→        if not files:
    40→            continue
    41→
    42→        batches.append(
    43→            {
    44→                "name": dimension,
    45→                "dimensions": [dimension],
    46→                "files_to_read": files,
    47→                "why": f"seed files for {dimension} review",
    48→            }
    49→        )
    50→
    51→    return batches
    52→
    53→
    54→def filter_batches_to_dimensions(
    55→    batches: list[dict],
    56→    dimensions: list[str],
    57→    *,
    58→    fallback_max_files: int | None = 80,
    59→) -> list[dict]:
    60→    """Keep only batches whose dimension is in the active set."""
    61→    selected = [dimension for dimension in dimensions if isinstance(dimension, str) and dimension]
    62→    if not selected:
    63→        return []
    64→    selected_set = set(selected)
    65→    filtered: list[dict] = []
    66→    covered: set[str] = set()
    67→    for batch in batches:
    68→        batch_dims = [dim for dim in batch.get("dimensions", []) if dim in selected_set]
    69→        if not batch_dims:
    70→            continue
    71→        filtered.append({**batch, "dimensions": batch_dims})
    72→        covered.update(batch_dims)
    73→
    74→    missing = [dim for dim in selected if dim not in covered]
    75→    if not missing:
    76→        return filtered
    77→
    78→    max_files = fallback_max_files if isinstance(fallback_max_files, int) else None
    79→    if isinstance(max_files, int) and max_files <= 0:
    80→        max_files = None
    81→    fallback_files = _collect_files_from_batches(
    82→        filtered or batches,
    83→        max_files=max_files,
    84→    )
    85→    if not fallback_files:
    86→        return filtered
    87→
    88→    for dim in missing:
    89→        filtered.append(
    90→            {
    91→                "name": dim,
    92→                "dimensions": [dim],
    93→                "files_to_read": fallback_files,
    94→                "why": f"no direct batch mapping for {dim}; using representative files",
    95→            }
    96→        )
    97→    return filtered
    98→
    99→
   100→def batch_concerns(
   101→    concerns: list,
   102→    *,
   103→    max_files: int | None = None,
   104→    active_dimensions: list[str] | None = None,
   105→) -> dict | None:
   106→    """Build investigation batch from mechanical concern signals."""
   107→    del active_dimensions
   108→    if not concerns:
   109→        return None
   110→
   111→    types = sorted({concern.type for concern in concerns if concern.type})
   112→    why_parts = ["mechanical detectors identified structural patterns needing judgment"]
   113→    if types:
   114→        why_parts.append(f"concern types: {', '.join(types)}")
   115→
   116→    files: list[str] = []
   117→    seen: set[str] = set()
   118→    concern_signals: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   119→    for concern in concerns:
   120→        candidate = _normalize_file_path(getattr(concern, "file", ""))
   121→        if not candidate or candidate in seen:
   122→            continue
   123→        seen.add(candidate)
   124→        files.append(candidate)
   125→
   126→        evidence_raw = getattr(concern, "evidence", ())
   127→        evidence = [
   128→            str(entry).strip()
   129→            for entry in evidence_raw
   130→            if isinstance(entry, str) and entry.strip()
   131→        ][:4]
   132→        summary = str(getattr(concern, "summary", "")).strip()
   133→        question = str(getattr(concern, "question", "")).strip()
   134→        concern_type = str(getattr(concern, "type", "")).strip()
   135→        fingerprint = str(getattr(concern, "fingerprint", "")).strip()
   136→        source_issues = tuple(
   137→            str(sid)
   138→            for sid in getattr(concern, "source_issues", ())
   139→            if isinstance(sid, str) and sid
   140→        )
   141→        signal: dict[str, object] = {
   142→            "type": concern_type or "design_concern",
   143→            "file": candidate,
   144→            "summary": summary or "Mechanical concern requires subjective judgment",
   145→            "question": question or "Is this pattern intentional or debt?",
   146→            "evidence": evidence,
   147→        }
   148→        if fingerprint:
   149→            signal["fingerprint"] = fingerprint
   150→        if source_issues:
   151→            signal["finding_ids"] = list(source_issues)
   152→        concern_signals.append(signal)
   153→
   154→    total_candidate_files = len(files)
   155→    if (
   156→        max_files is not None
   157→        and isinstance(max_files, int)
   158→        and max_files > 0
   159→        and total_candidate_files > max_files
   160→    ):
   161→        files = files[:max_files]
   162→        why_parts.append(
   163→            f"truncated to {max_files} files from {total_candidate_files} candidates"
   164→        )
   165→
   166→    # Build per-detector judgment finding counts by extracting the detector name
   167→    # from each source issue ID (format: "detector::file::detail").
   168→    detector_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   169→    seen_source_ids: set[str] = set()
   170→    for concern in concerns:
   171→        for sid in getattr(concern, "source_issues", ()):
   172→            sid_str = str(sid)
   173→            if sid_str in seen_source_ids:
   174→                continue
   175→            seen_source_ids.add(sid_str)
   176→            detector = sid_str.split("::", 1)[0] if "::" in sid_str else ""
   177→            if detector:
   178→                detector_counts[detector] = detector_counts.get(detector, 0) + 1
   179→
   180→    result: dict[str, object] = {
   181→        "name": "design_coherence",
   182→        "dimensions": ["design_coherence"],
   183→        "files_to_read": files,
   184→        "why": "; ".join(why_parts),
   185→        "total_candidate_files": total_candidate_files,
   186→        "concern_signals": concern_signals,
   187→        "concern_signal_count": len(concern_signals),
   188→    }
   189→    if detector_counts:
   190→        result["judgment_finding_counts"] = detector_counts
   191→    return result
   192→
   193→
   194→# Mechanical detectors → subjective dimensions they provide evidence for.
   195→# Mirrors _DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS in engine/_state/merge.py.
   196→_DETECTOR_DIMENSIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
   197→    "structural": ("design_coherence", "abstraction_fitness"),
   198→    "smells": ("design_coherence", "error_consistency"),
   199→    "global_mutable_config": ("initialization_coupling",),
   200→    "coupling": ("cross_module_architecture",),
   201→    "layer_violation": ("cross_module_architecture",),
   202→    "private_imports": ("cross_module_architecture",),
   203→    "dupes": ("convention_outlier",),
   204→    "boilerplate_duplication": ("convention_outlier",),
   205→    "naming": ("convention_outlier", "naming_quality"),
   206→    "flat_dirs": ("package_organization",),
   207→    "orphaned": ("design_coherence",),
   208→    "uncalled_functions": ("design_coherence",),
   209→    "responsibility_cohesion": ("design_coherence", "abstraction_fitness"),
   210→    "cycles": ("cross_module_architecture", "dependency_health"),
   211→    "dict_keys": ("type_safety",),
   212→    "props": ("abstraction_fitness",),
   213→    "signature": ("convention_outlier",),
   214→    "security": ("error_consistency",),
   215→    "facade": ("abstraction_fitness",),
   216→    "patterns": ("convention_outlier",),
   217→    "react": ("design_coherence",),
   218→    "single_use": ("abstraction_fitness",),
   219→}
   220→
   221→# Invert to dimension → set of detectors.
   222→_DIMENSION_DETECTORS: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
   223→for _det, _dims in _DETECTOR_DIMENSIONS.items():
   224→    for _dim in _dims:
   225→        _DIMENSION_DETECTORS.setdefault(_dim, set()).add(_det)
   226→
   227→
   228→def annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings(
   229→    batches: list[dict],
   230→    state: dict,
   231→) -> None:
   232→    """Add per-dimension judgment_finding_counts to batches that lack them.
   233→
   234→    For each batch, look at its dimension(s), find which detectors map to those
   235→    dimensions, count open judgment findings per detector from state, and inject
   236→    ``judgment_finding_counts`` so the prompt renderer can show CLI exploration
   237→    commands.  Batches that already have ``judgment_finding_counts`` (e.g. the
   238→    design_coherence concern batch) are left untouched.
   239→    """
   240→    from desloppify.base.registry import JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   241→
   242→    issues = state.get("issues")
   243→    if not isinstance(issues, dict):
   244→        return
   245→
   246→    # Count open judgment findings per detector once.
   247→    global_detector_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   248→    for issue in issues.values():
   249→        if not isinstance(issue, dict):
   250→            continue
   251→        status = str(issue.get("status", "")).strip()
   252→        if status not in ("open", "reopened"):
   253→            continue
   254→        detector = str(issue.get("detector", "")).strip()
   255→        if detector and detector in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS:
   256→            global_detector_counts[detector] = global_detector_counts.get(detector, 0) + 1
   257→
   258→    if not global_detector_counts:
   259→        return
   260→
   261→    for batch in batches:
   262→        if batch.get("judgment_finding_counts"):
   263→            continue
   264→        dims = batch.get("dimensions", [])
   265→        if not isinstance(dims, list):
   266→            continue
   267→        # Collect detectors relevant to this batch's dimensions.
   268→        relevant_detectors: set[str] = set()
   269→        for dim in dims:
   270→            relevant_detectors.update(_DIMENSION_DETECTORS.get(dim, ()))
   271→        if not relevant_detectors:
   272→            continue
   273→        counts = {
   274→            det: count
   275→            for det, count in global_detector_counts.items()
   276→            if det in relevant_detectors
   277→        }
   278→        if counts:
   279→            batch["judgment_finding_counts"] = counts
   280→
   281→
   282→__all__ = [
   283→    "annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings",
   284→    "batch_concerns",
   285→    "build_investigation_batches",
   286→    "filter_batches_to_dimensions",
   287→]

     2→

     5→import ast
     6→from collections import defaultdict
     7→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     8→
     9→
    10→@dataclass
    11→class TrackedDict:
    12→    """A dict variable tracked within a single scope."""
    13→
    14→    name: str
    15→    created_line: int
    16→    locally_created: bool
    17→    returned_or_passed: bool = False
    18→    has_dynamic_key: bool = False
    19→    has_star_unpack: bool = False
    20→    writes: dict[str, list[int]] = field(default_factory=lambda: defaultdict(list))
    21→    reads: dict[str, list[int]] = field(default_factory=lambda: defaultdict(list))
    22→    bulk_read: bool = False
    23→
    24→
    25→_CONFIG_NAMES = {
    26→    "config",
    27→    "settings",
    28→    "defaults",
    29→    "options",
    30→    "kwargs",
    31→    "context",
    32→    "ctx",
    33→    "env",
    34→    "params",
    35→    "metadata",
    36→    "headers",
    37→    "attrs",
    38→    "attributes",
    39→    "props",
    40→    "properties",
    41→}
    42→
    43→_READ_METHODS = {"get", "pop", "setdefault", "__getitem__", "__contains__"}
    44→_WRITE_METHODS = {"update", "setdefault", "__setitem__"}
    45→_BULK_READ_METHODS = {"keys", "values", "items", "copy", "__iter__"}
    46→
    47→
    48→def _levenshtein(s1: str, s2: str) -> int:
    49→    """Compute Levenshtein edit distance between two strings."""
    50→    if len(s1) < len(s2):
    51→        return _levenshtein(s2, s1)
    52→    if len(s2) == 0:
    53→        return len(s1)
    54→    prev = list(range(len(s2) + 1))
    55→    for i, c1 in enumerate(s1):
    56→        curr = [i + 1]
    57→        for j, c2 in enumerate(s2):
    58→            cost = 0 if c1 == c2 else 1
    59→            curr.append(min(curr[j] + 1, prev[j + 1] + 1, prev[j] + cost))
    60→        prev = curr
    61→    return prev[-1]
    62→
    63→
    64→def _is_singular_plural(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    65→    """Check if a and b are singular/plural variants of each other."""
    66→    return (
    67→        a + "s" == b
    68→        or b + "s" == a
    69→        or a + "es" == b
    70→        or b + "es" == a
    71→        or (a.endswith("ies") and a[:-3] + "y" == b)
    72→        or (b.endswith("ies") and b[:-3] + "y" == a)
    73→    )
    74→
    75→
    76→def _get_name(node: ast.expr) -> str | None:
    77→    """Extract variable name from a Name or Attribute(self.x) node."""
    78→    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
    79→        return node.id
    80→    if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Name):
    81→        return f"{node.value.id}.{node.attr}"
    82→    return None
    83→
    84→
    85→def _get_str_key(node: ast.expr) -> str | None:
    86→    """Extract a string literal from a subscript slice."""
    87→    if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, str):
    88→        return node.value
    89→    return None
    90→

    19→def detect_prop_interface_bloat(
    20→    path: Path, *, threshold: int = 14
    21→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:

    23→
    24→    Returns (entries, total_interfaces_checked).
    25→    """

    29→    _BLOAT_SUFFIXES = r"(?:Props|Context|ContextValue|ContextType|State|StateValue)\w*"
    30→    interface_re = re.compile(
    31→        rf"(?:export\s+)?(?:interface|type)\s+(\w+{_BLOAT_SUFFIXES})\s*(?:=\s*)?{{",

    35→    for filepath in find_ts_and_tsx_files(path):

    42→            content = p.read_text()
    43→            for m in interface_re.finditer(content):
    44→                total_interfaces += 1
    45→                name = m.group(1)
    46→                start = m.end()
    47→                # Count properties by issue the closing brace
    48→                brace_depth = 1
    49→                pos = start
    50→                prop_count = 0
    51→                while pos < len(content) and brace_depth > 0:
    52→                    ch = content[pos]
    53→                    if ch == "{":
    54→                        brace_depth += 1
    55→                    elif ch == "}":
    56→                        brace_depth -= 1
    57→                    elif ch == "\n" and brace_depth == 1:
    58→                        # Count non-empty, non-comment lines as properties
    59→                        line_start = pos + 1
    60→                        line_end = content.find("\n", line_start)
    61→                        if line_end == -1:
    62→                            line_end = len(content)
    63→                        line = content[line_start:line_end].strip()
    64→                        if (
    65→                            line
    66→                            and not line.startswith("//")
    67→                            and not line.startswith("*")
    68→                            and not line.startswith("/**")
    69→                            and line != "}"
    70→                        ):
    71→                            prop_count += 1
    72→                    pos += 1
    73→
    74→                if prop_count > threshold:
    75→                    kind = (
    76→                        "context"
    77→                        if "Context" in name
    78→                        else "state"
    79→                        if "State" in name
    80→                        else "props"

1→"""Mixed concerns detection (UI + data fetching + transforms in one file)."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import json
     6→import logging
     7→import re
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→from typing import Any
    10→
    11→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import rel
    12→
    13→from desloppify.base.discovery.source import find_tsx_files
    14→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    15→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize, print_table
    16→from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root
    17→
    18→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    19→
    20→
    21→def detect_mixed_concerns(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]:
    22→    """Find files that mix UI rendering with data fetching, state management, and business logic.
    23→
    24→    Heuristic: a .tsx file that has both JSX returns AND direct API/supabase calls
    25→    or both UI components AND heavy data transformation.
    26→
    27→    Returns (entries, total_files_checked).
    28→    """
    29→    files = find_tsx_files(path)
    30→    entries = []
    31→    for filepath in files:
    32→        try:
    33→            p = (
    34→                Path(filepath)
    35→                if Path(filepath).is_absolute()
    36→                else get_project_root() / filepath
    37→            )
    38→            content = p.read_text()
    39→            loc = len(content.splitlines())
    40→            if loc < 100:
    41→                continue
    42→
    43→            concerns = []
    44→
    45→            # UI rendering
    46→            has_jsx = bool(re.search(r"return\s*\(?\s*<", content))
    47→            if has_jsx:
    48→                concerns.append("jsx_rendering")
    49→
    50→            # Data fetching
    51→            has_fetch = bool(
    52→                re.search(r"useQuery|useMutation|supabase\.|fetch\(|axios", content)
    53→            )
    54→            if has_fetch:
    55→                concerns.append("data_fetching")
    56→
    57→            # Direct supabase calls (should be in hooks/services)
    58→            has_supabase = bool(re.search(r"supabase\.\w+\.\w+\.\w+", content))
    59→            if has_supabase:
    60→                concerns.append("direct_supabase")
    61→
    62→            # Heavy data transformation
    63→            transform_patterns = len(
    64→                re.findall(r"\.(map|filter|reduce|sort|flatMap)\s*\(", content)
    65→            )
    66→            if transform_patterns >= 3:
    67→                concerns.append(f"data_transforms({transform_patterns})")
    68→
    69→            # Event handler definitions (>5 = probably doing too much)
    70→            handler_count = len(re.findall(r"(?:const|function)\s+handle\w+", content))
    71→            if handler_count >= 5:
    72→                concerns.append(f"handlers({handler_count})")
    73→
    74→            # Flag if 3+ concern types in one file
    75→            if len(concerns) >= 3:
    76→                entries.append(
    77→                    {
    78→                        "file": filepath,
    79→                        "loc": loc,
    80→                        "concerns": concerns,
    81→                        "concern_count": len(concerns),
    82→                    }
    83→                )
    84→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
    85→            log_best_effort_failure(
    86→                logger, f"read TSX concern candidate {filepath}", exc
    87→            )
    88→            continue
    89→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["concern_count"]), len(files)
    90→
    91→
    92→def cmd_concerns(args: Any) -> None:
    93→    entries, _ = detect_mixed_concerns(Path(args.path))
    94→    if args.json:
    95→        print(json.dumps({"count": len(entries), "entries": entries}, indent=2))
    96→        return
    97→    if not entries:
    98→        print(colorize("No mixed-concern files found.", "green"))
    99→        return
   100→    print(colorize(f"\nMixed concerns: {len(entries)} files\n", "bold"))

### 3. **Review Guidance & Custom Prompts**

Each language defines `REVIEW_GUIDANCE` with language-specific patterns, auth checks, and naming conventions:

- **Python guidance** includes: async functions without await, bare except clauses, @lru_cache misuse, subprocess without timeout, mutable class attributes, @all__ checks, auth decorator consistency
- **TypeScript guidance** includes: useEffect dependencies, setTimeout for sync, React prop drilling (>15 props), dangerouslySetInnerHTML, useRef overuse, Context nesting (>5 deep), Supabase RLS bypass patterns
- **Go/Dart/GDScript** include minimal patterns-based guidance (no React/auth specifics)
- **C#** includes: async methods without await, oversized services, static mutable state, duplicate business rules, auth [Authorize] consistency

## Refactor Plan: Reviewer Finding Adjudication Flow

### Problem Summary

Three distinct problems intertwined:

1. **Duplicated detector-to-dimension mapping**: `_DETECTOR_DIMENSIONS` in `prepare_batches_builders.py` is a superset of `_DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS` in `merge.py`. The comment says "mirrors" but they've drifted — the reviewer mapping has 30 entries while the staleness mapping has 14. They serve different purposes but share a common core.

2. **Post-hoc mutation**: `annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings()` is called after batch construction in `prepare_holistic_orchestration.py` (line 291) to patch `judgment_finding_counts` and `mechanical_finding_counts` onto batch dicts. This is a separate code path from `batch_concerns()` which bakes `judgment_finding_counts` directly into the design_coherence batch at construction time.

3. **Prompt rendering complexity**: `render_judgment_findings_section()` has branching logic for judgment vs. mechanical counts, and conditionally changes its tail text based on whether `concern_signals` exist. This is conflating two rendering jobs.

### Design

#### Step 1: Add `subjective_dimensions` to `DetectorMeta` in `registry_catalog_models.py`

The `DetectorMeta` dataclass already has `dimension` (the *scoring* dimension like "Code quality") and `marks_dims_stale`. Add a new field:

```python
subjective_dimensions: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # Subjective review dimensions this detector provides evidence for
```

This is the canonical single source of truth. It lives in `base/` so both `engine/` and `intelligence/` can import it.

#### Step 2: Populate the field in `registry_catalog_entries.py`

For each detector entry that currently appears in either `_DETECTOR_DIMENSIONS` or `_DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS`, add the `subjective_dimensions` kwarg. Use the superset values from `_DETECTOR_DIMENSIONS` (the reviewer mapping), since it's the more complete one. Example:

```python
"structural": DetectorMeta(
    ...,
    subjective_dimensions=("design_coherence", "abstraction_fitness", "logic_clarity"),
    marks_dims_stale=True,
),
```

The staleness mapping (`merge.py`) currently only maps `structural` to `("design_coherence", "abstraction_fitness")` — missing `logic_clarity`. This is fine: `_mark_stale_on_mechanical_change` is gated by `marks_dims_stale=True` and only marks *existing* assessments stale. The superset is safe — if `logic_clarity` has never been assessed, it won't be touched.

#### Step 3: Add two derived helpers to `registry.py`

```python
def detector_subjective_dimensions() -> dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
    """Detector name -> subjective dimensions it provides evidence for."""
    return {
        name: meta.subjective_dimensions
        for name, meta in _REGISTRY.detectors.items()
        if meta.subjective_dimensions
    }

def dimension_to_detectors() -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    """Subjective dimension -> set of detector names that provide evidence."""
    result: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for name, meta in _REGISTRY.detectors.items():
        for dim in meta.subjective_dimensions:
            result.setdefault(dim, set()).add(name)
    return result
```

These are computed on demand from the registry, not cached module-level dicts. The registry is small (30-ish entries), so no performance concern.

#### Step 4: Delete `_DETECTOR_DIMENSIONS` and `_DIMENSION_DETECTORS` from `prepare_batches_builders.py`

Replace with imports from `registry.py`:

```python
from desloppify.base.registry import JUDGMENT_DETECTORS, detector_subjective_dimensions, dimension_to_detectors
```

In `annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings()`, replace `_DIMENSION_DETECTORS.get(dim, ())` with `dim_detectors.get(dim, ())` where `dim_detectors = dimension_to_detectors()`.

#### Step 5: Delete `_DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS` from `merge.py`

Replace with:

```python
from desloppify.base.registry import detector_subjective_dimensions
```

In `_mark_stale_on_mechanical_change()`, replace:
```python
dims = _DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS.get(detector)
```
with:
```python
dims = detector_subjective_dimensions().get(detector)
```

The safety fallback (lines 82-88) for detectors that haven't declared fine-grained dimension mappings remains unchanged — it still applies when `dims` is empty/None.

#### Step 6: Fold finding count annotation into batch construction

Instead of the post-hoc `annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings()` call in `prepare_holistic_orchestration.py` (lines 289-293), move the finding count logic into `build_investigation_batches()` in `prepare_batches_builders.py`. This means `build_investigation_batches` needs access to `state`.

Change the signature:

```python
def build_investigation_batches(
    holistic_ctx,
    lang: object,
    *,
    repo_root: Path | None = None,
    max_files_per_batch: int | None = None,
    state: dict | None = None,  # NEW
) -> list[dict]:
```

After building each batch dict, if `state` is provided, compute and attach `judgment_finding_counts` and `mechanical_finding_counts` inline. Extract the counting logic from `annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings` into a private helper `_count_findings_for_dimensions(state, dimensions)` that returns `(j_counts, m_counts)`.

Then delete `annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings()` entirely. Delete its call in `prepare_holistic_orchestration.py` (lines 289-293). Delete it from `__all__`.

The `batch_concerns()` function already bakes `judgment_finding_counts` into its output — no change needed there.

**Threading `state` through**: `prepare_holistic_review_payload` already has `state` and calls `deps.build_investigation_batches_fn()`. Just add `state=state` to that call (line 216-220 in `prepare_holistic_orchestration.py`).

#### Step 7: Simplify `render_judgment_findings_section`

Currently this function handles four permutations: judgment-only, mechanical-only, both, and the concern_signals tail. Simplify to a single concept: "relevant findings for this dimension."

```python
def render_findings_exploration_section(batch: dict[str, object]) -> str:
    """Render CLI exploration commands for detector findings relevant to this batch."""
    j_counts = batch.get("judgment_finding_counts")
    m_counts = batch.get("mechanical_finding_counts")
    all_counts = {}
    if isinstance(j_counts, dict):
        all_counts.update(j_counts)
    if isinstance(m_counts, dict):
        all_counts.update(m_counts)
    if not all_counts:
        return ""

    lines = [
        "RELEVANT FINDINGS — explore with CLI:",
        "These detectors found patterns related to this dimension. Use the commands below",
        "to explore the findings, then read the actual source code.",
        "",
    ]
    _render_detector_counts(all_counts, lines)
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(
        "Use these as starting points for investigation. Report actionable issues in issues[]."
    )
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"
```

The distinction between "judgment" and "mechanical" findings is irrelevant to the reviewer prompt — the reviewer doesn't care *why* they should look at the findings. The concern signals section (`render_mechanical_concern_signals`) already has its own explicit confirm/dismiss instructions and is rendered separately. The judgment_findings_section was trying to provide *different* confirm/dismiss instructions for the non-concern case, which is confusing.

Rename `render_judgment_findings_section` to `render_findings_exploration_section`. Update the two callers:
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/batch/prompt_template.py` (line 117)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/external.py` (line 237)

Both callers import the function by name, so update the imports. Also update `__all__` in `prompt_sections.py`.

#### Step 8: Update tests

- Tests in `test_prompt_sections.py` that reference `render_judgment_findings_section` need renaming to the new function name.
- Tests in `test_holistic_review.py` for `batch_concerns` are unchanged since that function is untouched.
- Add a small test in an appropriate test file (or the existing `test_holistic_review.py`) that verifies `detector_subjective_dimensions()` and `dimension_to_detectors()` return the right shape and cover expected detectors.

### What does NOT change

- `batch_concerns()` — untouched. It's the design_coherence-specific concern signal builder and already works correctly.
- `render_mechanical_concern_signals()` — untouched. Concern signals with fingerprints/dismiss/confirm are a design_coherence feature.
- The concern signal flow in `_append_concerns_batch` — untouched.
- `HolisticPrepareDependencies` — the `build_investigation_batches_fn` signature changes slightly (adds optional `state` kwarg), but this is backward-compatible.

### Net effect

- **Deleted**: `_DETECTOR_DIMENSIONS` dict (30 lines), `_DIMENSION_DETECTORS` computed dict (4 lines), `_DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS` dict (16 lines), `annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings()` function (65 lines), its try/except call site (5 lines), ~20 lines of branching logic in the old `render_judgment_findings_section`.
- **Added**: one `tuple[str, ...]` field on `DetectorMeta`, ~30 `subjective_dimensions=()` kwargs across catalog entries, two ~8-line helper functions in `registry.py`, ~15-line `_count_findings_for_dimensions` helper.
- **Net**: roughly 80 lines deleted, 60 added. One source of truth instead of two divergent copies. Finding counts baked into batch construction instead of patched on. Cleaner prompt rendering.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/base/registry_catalog_models.py` - Add `subjective_dimensions` field to `DetectorMeta`
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/base/registry_catalog_entries.py` - Populate `subjective_dimensions` on each detector entry

   209→    "naming": ("convention_outlier", "naming_quality"),
   210→    "flat_dirs": ("package_organization",),
   211→    "orphaned": ("design_coherence",),
   212→    "uncalled_functions": ("design_coherence",),
   213→    "responsibility_cohesion": ("design_coherence", "abstraction_fitness"),
   214→    "cycles": ("cross_module_architecture", "dependency_health"),
   215→    "dict_keys": ("type_safety",),

   223→    # --- mechanical detectors (context for reviewer, not adjudication) ---
   224→    "test_coverage": ("test_strategy",),

   228→    "unused_enums": ("design_coherence",),
   229→    "logs": ("logic_clarity",),
   230→}
   231→
   232→# Invert to dimension → set of detectors.
   233→_DIMENSION_DETECTORS: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
   234→for _det, _dims in _DETECTOR_DIMENSIONS.items():
   235→    for _dim in _dims:
   236→        _DIMENSION_DETECTORS.setdefault(_dim, set()).add(_det)
   237→
   238→
   239→def annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings(
   240→    batches: list[dict],
   241→    state: dict,
   242→) -> None:
   243→    """Add per-dimension finding counts to batches that lack them.
   244→
   245→    For each batch, look at its dimension(s), find which detectors map to those
   246→    dimensions, count open findings per detector from state, and inject
   247→    ``judgment_finding_counts`` (judgment detectors — confirm/dismiss) and
   248→    ``mechanical_finding_counts`` (non-judgment — contextual evidence) so the
   249→    prompt renderer can show CLI exploration commands.
   250→
   251→    Batches that already have ``judgment_finding_counts`` (e.g. the
   252→    design_coherence concern batch) are left untouched.
   253→    """
   254→    from desloppify.base.registry import JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   255→
   256→    issues = state.get("issues")
   257→    if not isinstance(issues, dict):
   258→        return
   259→
   260→    # Count open findings per detector once, split by judgment vs mechanical.
   261→    judgment_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   262→    mechanical_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   263→    for issue in issues.values():
   264→        if not isinstance(issue, dict):
   265→            continue
   266→        status = str(issue.get("status", "")).strip()
   267→        if status not in ("open", "reopened"):
   268→            continue
   269→        detector = str(issue.get("detector", "")).strip()
   270→        if not detector:
   271→            continue
   272→        target = judgment_counts if detector in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS else mechanical_counts
   273→        target[detector] = target.get(detector, 0) + 1
   274→
   275→    if not judgment_counts and not mechanical_counts:
   276→        return
   277→
   278→    for batch in batches:
   279→        if batch.get("judgment_finding_counts"):
   280→            continue
   281→        dims = batch.get("dimensions", [])
   282→        if not isinstance(dims, list):
   283→            continue
   284→        # Collect detectors relevant to this batch's dimensions.
   285→        relevant_detectors: set[str] = set()
   286→        for dim in dims:
   287→            relevant_detectors.update(_DIMENSION_DETECTORS.get(dim, ()))
   288→        if not relevant_detectors:
   289→            continue
   290→        j_counts = {
   291→            det: count
   292→            for det, count in judgment_counts.items()
   293→            if det in relevant_detectors
   294→        }
   295→        m_counts = {
   296→            det: count
   297→            for det, count in mechanical_counts.items()
   298→            if det in relevant_detectors
   299→        }
   300→        if j_counts:
   301→            batch["judgment_finding_counts"] = j_counts
   302→        if m_counts:
   303→            batch["mechanical_finding_counts"] = m_counts
   304→
   305→
   306→__all__ = [
   307→    "annotate_batches_with_judgment_findings",
   308→    "batch_concerns",
   309→    "build_investigation_batches",
   310→    "filter_batches_to_dimensions",
   311→]

    58→def _mark_stale_on_mechanical_change(
    59→    state: StateModel,
    60→    *,
    61→    changed_detectors: set[str],
    62→    now: str,
    63→) -> None:
    64→    """Mark subjective assessments stale when mechanical issues change.
    65→
    66→    Only marks dimensions that already have an assessment — doesn't create
    67→    new entries for dimensions that have never been reviewed.
    68→    """
    69→    assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments")
    70→    if not isinstance(assessments, dict) or not assessments:
    71→        return
    72→
    73→    affected_dims: set[str] = set()
    74→    for detector in changed_detectors:
    75→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
    76→        if meta is None or not meta.marks_dims_stale:
    77→            continue
    78→        dims = _DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS.get(detector)
    79→        if dims:
    80→            affected_dims.update(dims)
    81→            continue
    82→        # Safety fallback for newly added "marks_dims_stale" detectors that
    83→        # have not declared fine-grained dimension mappings yet.
    84→        affected_dims.update(
    85→            dim
    86→            for dim in assessments
    87→            if isinstance(dim, str) and dim.strip()
    88→        )
    89→
    90→    if not affected_dims:
    91→        return
    92→
    93→    for dimension in sorted(affected_dims):
    94→        if dimension not in assessments:
    95→            continue
    96→        payload = assessments[dimension]
    97→        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
    98→            continue
    99→        # Don't overwrite if already stale
   100→        if payload.get("needs_review_refresh"):
   101→            continue
   102→        payload["needs_review_refresh"] = True
   103→        payload["refresh_reason"] = "mechanical_issues_changed"
   104→        payload["stale_since"] = now
   105→

   107→@dataclass
   108→class MergeScanOptions:
   109→    """Configuration bundle for merging a scan into persisted state."""
   110→
   111→    lang: str | None = None
   112→    scan_path: str | None = None
   113→    force_resolve: bool = False
   114→    exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()
   115→    potentials: dict[str, int] | None = None
   116→    merge_potentials: bool = False
   117→    codebase_metrics: dict[str, Any] | None = None
   118→    include_slow: bool = True
   119→    ignore: list[str] | None = None
   120→    subjective_integrity_target: float | None = None
   121→
   122→
   123→def merge_scan(
   124→    state: StateModel,
   125→    current_issues: list[dict],
   126→    options: MergeScanOptions | None = None,
   127→) -> ScanDiff:
   128→    """Merge a fresh scan into existing state and return a diff summary."""
   129→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   130→    resolved_options = options or MergeScanOptions()
   131→
   132→    now = utc_now()
   133→    _record_scan_metadata(
   134→        state,
   135→        now,
   136→        lang=resolved_options.lang,
   137→        include_slow=resolved_options.include_slow,
   138→        scan_path=resolved_options.scan_path,
   139→    )
   140→    _merge_scan_inputs(
   141→        state,
   142→        lang=resolved_options.lang,
   143→        potentials=resolved_options.potentials,
   144→        merge_potentials=resolved_options.merge_potentials,
   145→        codebase_metrics=resolved_options.codebase_metrics,
   146→    )
   147→
   148→    existing = state["issues"]
   149→    ignore_patterns = (
   150→        resolved_options.ignore
   151→        if resolved_options.ignore is not None
   152→        else state.get("config", {}).get("ignore", [])
   153→    )
   154→    current_ids, new_count, reopened_count, current_by_detector, ignored_count, upsert_changed = (
   155→        upsert_issues(
   156→            existing,
   157→            current_issues,
   158→            ignore_patterns,
   159→            now,
   160→            lang=resolved_options.lang,
   161→        )
   162→    )
   163→
   164→    raw_issues = len(current_issues)
   165→    suppressed_pct = _compute_suppression(raw_issues, ignored_count)
   166→
   167→    ran_detectors = (
   168→        set(resolved_options.potentials.keys())
   169→        if resolved_options.potentials is not None
   170→        else None
   171→    )
   172→    suspect_detectors = find_suspect_detectors(
   173→        existing,
   174→        current_by_detector,
   175→        resolved_options.force_resolve,
   176→        ran_detectors,
   177→    )
   178→    auto_resolved, skipped_other_lang, resolved_out_of_scope, resolve_changed = verify_disappeared(
   179→        existing,
   180→        current_ids,
   181→        suspect_detectors,
   182→        now,
   183→        lang=resolved_options.lang,
   184→        scan_path=resolved_options.scan_path,
   185→        exclude=resolved_options.exclude,
   186→    )
   187→
   188→    # Mark subjective assessments stale when mechanical issues changed.
   189→    changed_detectors = upsert_changed | resolve_changed
   190→    if changed_detectors:
   191→        _mark_stale_on_mechanical_change(
   192→            state, changed_detectors=changed_detectors, now=now,

   200→    _append_scan_history(

   108→def render_historical_focus(batch: dict[str, object]) -> str:

   150→def _concern_signal_lines(entry: dict[str, object]) -> list[str]:
   151→    """Render one concern signal entry into prompt lines."""
   152→    file = str(entry.get("file", "")).strip() or "(unknown file)"
   153→    concern_type = str(entry.get("type", "")).strip() or "design_concern"
   154→    summary = str(entry.get("summary", "")).strip()
   155→    question = str(entry.get("question", "")).strip()
   156→    evidence_raw = entry.get("evidence", [])
   157→    evidence = (
   158→        [str(item).strip() for item in evidence_raw if isinstance(item, str) and item.strip()]
   159→        if isinstance(evidence_raw, list)
   160→        else []
   161→    )
   162→    lines = [f"  - [{concern_type}] {file}"]
   163→    if summary:
   164→        lines.append(f"    summary: {summary}")
   165→    if question:
   166→        lines.append(f"    question: {question}")
   167→    lines.extend(f"    evidence: {snippet}" for snippet in evidence[:2])
   168→    fingerprint = str(entry.get("fingerprint", "")).strip()
   169→    if fingerprint:
   170→        lines.append(f"    fingerprint: {fingerprint}")
   171→    return lines

   183→    signals = batch.get("concern_signals")
   184→    if not isinstance(signals, list) or not signals:

   189→    lines.append(

   207→    capped_signals = valid_signals[:30]
